subtitle: In the shadow of sultans, a doorway of hunger and song stays open

panels.shot: solemn mid-shot with deep background of Delhi’s silhouette at dusk
panels.action: Nizamuddin Auliya stands quietly at the threshold of a simple khanqah, city walls faint in the distance, his gaze calm yet watchful as poor travelers approach along a dusty path.

dialogue.text: In Chishti Delhi of the late thirteenth and early fourteenth century, while sultans ruled from fortresses, Nizamuddin Auliya opened a modest khanqah where hunger, sorrow and song crossed all boundaries.

i18n.hi: तेरहवीं के आख़िर और चौदहवीं सदी की शुरू की चिश्ती दिल्ली में, जब सुल्तान क़िलों से राज करते थे, निज़ामुद्दीन औलिया ने एक सादा ख़ानक़ाह खोली जहाँ भूख, ग़म और गीत हर सरहद पार कर जाते थे।

panels.shot: low-angle wide of Badaun’s streets with a small boy in foreground
panels.action: A young Nizamuddin, bareheaded and thin, walks through the lanes of Badaun, past modest brick houses and a distant mosque, clutching a small book to his chest.

dialogue.text: Nizamuddin was born in Badaun in 1238, in a world shaken by shifting dynasties and Mongol storms on the horizon, where learning and poverty often walked together.

i18n.hi: निज़ामुद्दीन 1238 में बदायूँ में पैदा हुए, एक ऐसे दौर में जब सल्तनतें बदल रही थीं, मंगोल तूफ़ान आकाश पर थे, और इल्म व ग़रीबी अक्सर साथ-साथ चलते थे।

panels.shot: intimate close-up indoors, lamplight on a youth’s face bent over texts
panels.action: Inside a dim room, a slightly older Nizamuddin studies Arabic and Persian texts by a small oil lamp, his expression intent, a clay bowl of simple food beside him.

dialogue.text: From his youth he turned to study and prayer, learning the words of law and scripture, yet feeling drawn toward a path where these words would touch the hungry and the forgotten.

i18n.hi: जवानी से ही वह पढ़ाई और नमाज़ में लगे, क़ानून और किताब के अल्फ़ाज़ सीखे, पर दिल उन्हें उस राह की तरफ़ खींचता रहा जहाँ यही अल्फ़ाज़ भूखों और भुला दिए गए लोगों तक पहुँचें।

panels.shot: wide shot of Delhi’s early Sultanate skyline as a lone traveler arrives
panels.action: Nizamuddin, now a young man, enters Delhi’s bustling outskirts, turbaned officials on horseback passing by as traders, artisans and mendicants crowd the road.

dialogue.text: Drawn by the promise of knowledge and masters of the soul, he came to Delhi, where the Sultanate’s power rose behind high walls and the barefoot poor filled its lanes.

i18n.hi: इल्म के वादे और रूह के उस्तादों के बुलावे से वह दिल्ली आए, जहाँ सल्तनत की ताक़त ऊँची दीवारों के पीछे उठ रही थी और नंगे पाँव ग़रीब गलियों में भर गए थे।

panels.shot: reverent medium shot inside a simple hujra with a teacher’s presence implied off-frame
panels.action: Seated humbly on the floor of a sparse cell, Nizamuddin listens, head bowed, to an unseen elder, his hands resting open in his lap as if receiving a trust.

dialogue.text: In Delhi he entered the circle of the Chishti saints, taking the path under the guidance of Baba Farid, where love of God was shown through service, song and distance from royal favor.

i18n.hi: दिल्ली में वह चिश्ती संतों की महफ़िल में दाख़िल हुए, बाबा फ़रीद की रहनुमाई में राह पकड़ी, जहाँ ख़ुदा की मोहब्बत ख़िदमत, क़व्वाली और शाही मेहर से दूर रहते हुए दिखाई जाती थी।

panels.shot: establishing wide of Ghiyaspur on the Yamuna’s edge, khanqah huts scattered
panels.action: On the edge of the city at Ghiyaspur, Nizamuddin stands among simple mud-walled buildings and trees near the river, a few disciples and poor visitors gathered around him.

dialogue.text: By the 1270s he settled at Ghiyaspur, turning a modest compound into a khanqah, where bread, counsel and music were offered to those from every quarter of Delhi’s divided society.

i18n.hi: 1270 के दशक तक वह ग़ियासपुर में टिक गए, एक सादा से अहाते को ख़ानक़ाह बना दिया, जहाँ रोटी, मशवरा और संगीत, दिल्ली के बँटे हुए समाज के हर कोने से आए लोगों को मिलता था।

panels.shot: busy interior wide of the khanqah courtyard, emphasis on shared eating
panels.action: Within the khanqah courtyard, Nizamuddin sits on a low platform as servants ladle food from large pots into bowls passed to artisans, peasants, widows and travellers seated side by side.

dialogue.text: The khanqah became a living institution: communal meals, shelter and listening ears, funded by gifts from patrons yet directed toward those who possessed little but need and a story to tell.

i18n.hi: ख़ानक़ाह एक ज़िंदा इदारा बन गई: सामूहिक खाना, आसरा और सुनने वाले कान, जो सख़ावत से चलती थी मगर रुख़ उन लोगों की तरफ़ रहता था जिनके पास ज़रूरत और कहानी के सिवा कुछ न था।

panels.shot: warm mid-shot of Nizamuddin listening to a supplicant, soft afternoon light
panels.action: Nizamuddin leans forward on his cushion, eyes gentle, as a weary man in coarse clothes speaks, his hands nervous, a line of others waiting in the background.

dialogue.text: Amir Hasan Sijzi later recorded these hours of counsel in Fawaid-ul-Fuad, where Nizamuddin’s words circled around poverty, patience, divine love and the duty to keep one’s door open.

i18n.hi: अमीर हसन सिज़्ज़ी ने बाद में इन नसीहतों की घड़ियाँ फवाइदुल फ़ुअाद में लिखीं, जहाँ निज़ामुद्दीन की बातें ग़रीबी, सब्र, इलाही मोहब्बत और दरवाज़ा खुला रखने की ज़िम्मेदारी के इर्द-गिर्द घूमती हैं।

panels.shot: low, intimate shot of a mehfil-e-samaa with listeners in silhouette
panels.action: In the khanqah hall at night, Nizamuddin sits among disciples as singers perform devotional verses, some swaying in feeling, others still, candles glowing against the dark.

dialogue.text: Music, sama, filled the gatherings, with poems of longing sung in Hindavi and Persian, even as jurists and officials argued about its lawfulness beyond the khanqah walls.

i18n.hi: समा की महफ़िलों में संगीत गूंजता था, हिनदवी और फ़ारसी में तड़प से भरी नज़्में गायी जातीं, जबकि फ़क़ीह और अमला ख़ानक़ाह की दीवारों के बाहर उसकी जाइज़ियत पर बहस करते रहते।

panels.shot: mid-shot of Nizamuddin surrounded by diverse visitors—Hindu, Muslim, stranger
panels.action: Men of varied dress—turbaned Muslim scholars, a Hindu artisan with tilak, wandering faqirs and veiled women—sit before Nizamuddin, forming a circle around him in the courtyard.

dialogue.text: In Ghiyaspur, lines of status and community blurred; the saint’s fame drew merchants, labourers, women and men of different faiths, all seeking words that might steady their hearts.

i18n.hi: ग़ियासपुर में रुतबे और बिरादरी की लकीरें धुंधली हो गईं; वली की शोहरत से सौदागर, मज़दूर, औरतें और अलग-अलग मजहबों के लोग आते, सब दिल थामने वाली बातों की तलाश में।

panels.shot: dramatic wide of city gate with royal envoys approaching the khanqah
panels.action: Armored riders and robed envoys bearing the Sultan’s insignia approach the simple gate of the khanqah, its unadorned walls contrasting with their polished harness.

dialogue.text: Sultans ruled nearby from fortified palaces. Their envoys came with invitations, threats and patronage, seeking to draw the Chishti shaykh into the orbit of courtly ambitions.

i18n.hi: पास ही सुल्तान मज़बूत महलों से राज करते थे। उनके नुमायंदे दावतों, धमकियों और सरपरस्ती के पैग़ाम लेकर आते, चिश्ती शेख़ को दरबार की ख़्वाहिशों के घेरे में खींचना चाहते।

panels.shot: measured mid-shot inside the khanqah with Nizamuddin facing an envoy
panels.action: Seated calmly indoors, Nizamuddin looks toward a richly dressed court official who stands, scroll in hand, while disciples watch tensely from the corners of the room.

dialogue.speaker: nizamuddin_auliya
dialogue.text: Our door is for the needy. Let the palace keep its distance.

i18n.hi: हमारा दरवाज़ा मुफ़लिसों के लिए है। महल दूर ही रहे।

panels.shot: tight close-up of Nizamuddin’s composed face after the envoy leaves
panels.action: The door behind him stands slightly open to the courtyard, but the room is quiet; Nizamuddin’s face shows calm resolve, his gaze lowered yet firm.

dialogue.text: He avoided formal ties and honours from rulers, not out of rebellion alone, but to protect the khanqah’s freedom to serve without being bent by palace demands.

i18n.hi: उन्होंने बादशाहों से रस्मी रिश्ते और इज़्ज़तें टाल दीं, सिर्फ़ बग़ावत में नहीं, बल्कि इस लिए कि ख़ानक़ाह की आज़ादी बची रहे, सेवा महल के हुक्म से न झुके।

panels.shot: wide shot of Delhi, with fortress and khanqah both visible across the landscape
panels.action: From a vantage point, Delhi stretches under a hazy sky: the Sultan’s citadel on one side, the modest cluster of Ghiyaspur on the other, paths of people threading between them.

dialogue.text: Simon Digby later wrote of this tension: saintly and royal authority facing each other, each commanding loyalty, the khanqah a quiet rival to the pomp of throne and army.

i18n.hi: सायमन डिग्बी ने बाद में इस तनाऊँ को लिखा: औलिया और बादशाहत आमने-सामने, दोनों वफ़ादारी माँगते, ख़ानक़ाह तख़्त और लश्कर की शान की ख़ामोश हम-आवाज़।

panels.shot: serene mid-shot of Nizamuddin distributing alms, a disciple carrying coins
panels.action: Nizamuddin sits as a disciple hands out coins and cloth to poor visitors, while a merchant in fine dress respectfully offers a pouch to support the khanqah’s work.

dialogue.text: The Chishti lodge was no dream floating above politics. Gifts from merchants, nobles and officials fed its kitchens, even as Nizamuddin urged his followers to live simply, owning little in their own names.

i18n.hi: चिश्ती आश्रम सियासत से ऊपर तैरता कोई सपना नहीं था। सौदागर, अमीर और अफ़सरों के तोहफ़े उसकी रसोई चलाते, जबकि निज़ामुद्दीन अपने मुरीदों को सादा रहने, नाम पर कम से कम चीज़ रखने की नसीहत करते।

panels.shot: muted interior shot, Nizamuddin teaching disciples seated in a circle
panels.action: Within a bare room, Nizamuddin speaks to attentive disciples, some taking notes on paper, others listening with hands folded, the air heavy with concentration.

dialogue.text: In Fawaid-ul-Fuad, we hear him teaching that true wealth is poverty before God, that service to the poor is greater than proximity to rulers, and that love must extend beyond one’s own circle.

i18n.hi: फवाइदुल फ़ुअाद में हम उन्हें सिखाते सुनते हैं कि असल दौलत ख़ुदा के सामने फ़क़्र है, कि ग़रीबों की ख़िदमत हाकिमों की क़ुरब से बड़ी है, और मोहब्बत अपनी मंडली से बाहर तक फैलनी चाहिए।

panels.shot: evening wide in the khanqah courtyard with pilgrims, qawwals and faqirs gathered
panels.action: At dusk, lamps flicker as qawwals tune instruments, faqirs assemble, and travellers from near and far settle in the courtyard around Nizamuddin’s quiet figure.

dialogue.text: By the early fourteenth century, Ghiyaspur had become a famed Chishti center, woven into Delhi’s daily life, where song, advice and shared meals reached beyond ethnicity, craft and creed.

i18n.hi: चौदहवीं सदी की शुरू तक ग़ियासपुर एक मशहूर चिश्ती मरकज़ बन चुका था, दिल्ली की रोज़मर्रा ज़िंदगी में बुना हुआ, जहाँ गीत, मशवरा और साँझा खाना नस्ल, पेशा और मज़हब की हदें पार करता था।

panels.shot: somber interior shot, Nizamuddin aged and frail, disciples close by
panels.action: An aged Nizamuddin reclines on a simple pallet, his beard white, disciples gathered respectfully, the atmosphere hushed as if aware that an era is closing.

dialogue.text: Nizamuddin died in Delhi on April 3, 1325, leaving behind no palace, no army, only a network of hearts bound by his insistence that a khanqah’s door must never shut against the needy.

i18n.hi: निज़ामुद्दीन 3 अप्रैल 1325 को दिल्ली में इंतिक़ाल कर गए, पीछे न कोई महल छोड़ा, न लश्कर, बस दिलों का वो जाल जो उनकी इस ज़िद से बँधा था कि ख़ानक़ाह का दरवाज़ा मुफ़लिसों पर कभी बंद न हो।

panels.shot: modern-day wide of the Nizamuddin Dargah area, old shrine amid living city
panels.action: The Nizamuddin Dargah stands amidst crowded alleys, present-day worshippers and visitors filling the courtyard, tall buildings of modern Delhi rising faintly beyond.

dialogue.text: Today the Nizamuddin Dargah still draws multitudes. His legacy lies in a kingdom without throne—where service, shared food and song remain the true measures of power in a restless city.

i18n.hi: आज निज़ामुद्दीन दरगाह अब भी हज़ूम खींचती है। उनकी विरासत एक बे-तख़्त सल्तनत में है—जहाँ ख़िदमत, बाँटा हुआ खाना और गीत ही बेक़रार शहर में ताक़त का असल पैमाना हैं।

title_i18n.hi: निज़ामुद्दीन ने ख़ानक़ाह का दरवाज़ा खोल दिया

subtitle_i18n.en: In the shadow of sultans, a doorway of hunger and song stays open
subtitle_i18n.hi: सुल्तानों की छाया में, भूख और गीत का एक दरवाज़ा हमेशा खुला रहा
